correctness.rationale: For the flat Klein quotient generated by (x+a,-y) and (x,y+b), deck parity yields d(P,Q)^2=min{u^2+r^2,(a-u)^2+w^2}, u in [0,a], where r,w are two circular distances. Their nondominated frontier has r+w=B=b-delta, |r-w|<=delta, delta=dist(2v,bZ). For fixed r,w, optimal horizontal u is the intersection of the two parabolas if inside [0,a], else an endpoint; maximization over t=|r-w| gives t=min{delta,a^2/B} and exact eccentricity E(v)^2=(a^2+B^2)/4+(1+B^2/a^2)t^2/4. Both branches strictly decrease with delta, so centers at delta=b/2 and maximum eccentricity at delta=0. Substitution yields radius a^2/b+b/4 for a<=b/2 or a/2+b^2/(8a) otherwise, diameter sqrt(a^2+b^2)/2, and area-normalized branch minima at ratios 1/(2sqrt3), sqrt3/2 with 2/(3sqrt3). Independently maximized the deck formula over six aspect pairs and 21 center levels, 126 grid/analytic tests with strict comparisons, and verified equality ratios symbolically. All claims refer to metric radius, not systole or injectivity radius. value.rationale: The minimax eccentricity (metric radius) of a compact flat Klein bottle and its area-normalization are natural intrinsic geometric quantities. A complete pointwise eccentricity profile, two distinct sharp area-optimal similarity classes and a farthest-point transition are motivated by flat geometry and differ genuinely from systolic optimization. They are not a mere special-value computation; the full moduli-space classification is essential.
